page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a centred heading and rule titles set apart. Running head and page number at the top. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.l: Sexta Regula.
Filij aut filiæ, ex pluribus fratribus aut sororibus
n[?]ati,natæve,quamvis numero inæquales sint, patruo
tamen defuncto, non in stirpes (ut quidam veterum
voluerunt) sed in capita succedunt. Secundum Bal-
dum & Salycetum in d.Auth. cessante. Et per Consti-
tutionem Caroli Quinti Imperatoris in Comitiis
Spirensibus, Anno 1529. promulgatam.Vide Schnei-
devvinum.
Septima Regula[?]
Post fratres fratrumq; filios, vocantur ad succes-
sionem reliqui collaterales, quicunq; in gradu sunt
proximiores, remotioribus exclusis: ita quòd infal-
libiliter semper prior in gradu, sit potior in succes-
sione, & pares in gradu, pariter admittantur in capi-
ta, secundum numerum personarum, non in stirpes.
Authen. post fratres.la.2. C. de legitimis hæredibus.
Obseruandum, quòd semper in computatione gra-
duum descendentes ex fratre ex altero tantum latere
sint remotiores, quàm descendentes à fatre[?], ex utroq;
parente conjuncti, inquit Schneidevvinus.
Sequentes Regulæ de Collateralium
naturalium tantum succes-
sione observen-
tur.
Prima Regula[?]
Fratres naturales tantùm, paterna origine conjun-
cti, sibi invicem non succedunt: quia nulla inter eos
agnatio, vel cognatio de jure intercedit. §. vulgò
quæsitos. inst. de successione cognator.
Secunda Regula[?]
Fratres naturales tantùm, respectu maternæ lineæ
conjuncti sibi invicem succedere queunt. l.1. & l. si-
purius.ff. unde cognati.

page.notes: The stray mark at the bottom centre is a printer's ornament or show-through, not text, and is left out. "Septima Regula", "Prima Regula" and "Secunda Regula" are printed with an ornamented R whose flourish looks like a question mark; marked [?]. "n[?]ati" is partly lost at the left edge of the line. "fatre" appears as printed; the first letter is damaged and may be "p". "Schneidevvinum" is kept as printed. The rule titles are treated as level 3 headings, the centred title above the rules as level 2.
